patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: The room won't stop spinning and I keep listing to one side when I try to walk. It came on all of a sudden this morning. It's 'just' dizziness, but it won't quit and I can't stay upright.
presentation.triageNote: 72-year-old male with sudden persistent spinning dizziness. He lists to one side, has marked truncal unsteadiness and direction-changing nystagmus, and cannot stand or walk without assistance.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because sudden persistent vertigo with inability to stand and direction-changing nystagmus is a high-risk central neurologic presentation.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This older adult has abrupt continuous vertigo, severe truncal instability, lateropulsion, direction-changing nystagmus, and inability to walk unaided.
clinical.acuityReason: The prominent gait and eye-movement abnormalities are not safely explained by uncomplicated peripheral vertigo and require rapid stroke assessment.
keyFindings: Cannot stand or walk without help
redFlags: Acute vestibular syndrome with inability to walk
teachingPoints: Severe truncal ataxia is a central warning sign even when limb weakness or speech change is absent.
Early non-contrast CT may miss posterior circulation ischemia.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Urgent stroke evaluation and appropriate imaging would likely lead to admission for neurologic monitoring and treatment.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: gripping the arm of the chair for balance, tilted to one side
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 72-year-old man who looks queasy, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: gripping the arm of the chair for balance, body tilted to one side. Expression: nauseated and off-balance. Clearly visible: a white-knuckle grip on the chair and an unsteady, tilted posture. No text, no logos.
